report.summary: Chunk 4 of dss.py: defines DSSResult dataclass and semantic_super_sample function with docstring claiming deterministic DSS v0 pipeline.
risks: semantic_super_sample | medium | docstring claims 'deterministic DSS v0 context-selection pipeline' but code includes floating-point operations (e.g., addition, multiplication) and dictionary iteration order (Python 3.7+ deterministic) – determinism is plausible but not enforced by code. Check for any non-deterministic dependencies (e.g., hash randomization).
semantic_super_sample | low | docstring does not specify that seed_scores with zero or negative scores are silently dropped (score > 0 check). Could be unexpected.

handoff.purpose: Defines DSSResult dataclass and semantic_super_sample function.

symbols.name: DSSResult
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding DSS pipeline results.

symbols.name: DSSResult.to_dict
symbols.note: Serializes DSSResult to a dictionary using SHA256 hashes and envelope method.

symbols.name: semantic_super_sample
symbols.note: Runs the deterministic DSS v0 context-selection pipeline.

claims.text: Run the deterministic DSS v0 context-selection pipeline.
claims.why: The claim of determinism cannot be fully verified from this chunk alone; it depends on external functions and the overall pipeline. Code appears deterministic given deterministic inputs and no random number generation visible, but external calls (e.g., build_forest_hierarchy, carry_temporal_scores, etc.) may introduce non-determinism.

claims.text: seed_scores items with score > 0 are kept; others raise KeyError if node_id not in file_ids, or are dropped if score <= 0.
claims.why: Code iterates over seed_scores, checks node_id in file_ids (raises KeyError if not), then calls _finite_non_negative (assumed to validate), and only adds to seeds dict if score > 0. So non-positive scores are dropped silently.

claims.text: temporal_weight is used to blend temporal scores into coarse_input.
claims.why: Code adds config.temporal_weight * score to coarse_input for each temporal score.

claims.text: restrict_scores, prolongate_scores, diffuse_relation_scores are called with the given parameters.
claims.why: These functions are called but defined outside this chunk; their behavior is not verifiable here.

claims.text: relation_weights are taken from config.weights() and unknown_relation_weight for missing relations.
claims.why: Code retrieves relation_weights = config.weights() and uses config.unknown_relation_weight for missing keys.

claims.text: final_scores are normalised by max value.
claims.why: Calls _normalise_max(fused); function not in this chunk.
build_context_plan is called but not defined here.

claims.text: receipt includes input_sha256 of sorted input values.
claims.why: Code creates input_values dict with sorted items and computes _digest for each.

claims.text: receipt includes branch_selection with selected and pruned nodes from prolongation.
claims.why: Code constructs branch_selection dict from prolongation attributes.

claims.text: receipt includes relation_channels with digests of channel dicts.
claims.why: Code creates dict mapping channel.relation to _digest(channel.to_dict()).

claims.text: returned DSSResult contains all pipeline outputs.
claims.why: Return statement constructs DSSResult with all listed fields.

observations.what: Docstring claims deterministic pipeline; code uses floating-point arithmetic and dictionary iteration which are deterministic in CPython 3.7+, but external functions may introduce non-determinism.
seed_scores with score <= 0 are silently dropped; this is not documented in the docstring.
The function raises KeyError for unknown node IDs in seed_scores; this is a change from previous behavior? Not checkable.
to_dict uses hierarchy.content_sha256 and receipt.envelope(); these methods are not defined in this chunk.
